entries.operation: CNB's loader registry, and the native content manager it needs
entries.evidence: measured rather than deferred on style. The registry itself works: a C probe mints a custom asset type id from a name, registers a loader, writes a .cnb of that type, and cna_content_manager_load_foreign_ext calls the loader and hands the object back -- twice for the same name, from the cache, without calling the loader again, which is XNA reference-type caching. What blocks the projection is this binding's own architecture: that retrieval route takes a NATIVE content manager handle, and there is none here. ContentManager in this package is a managed XNB reader that opens the file through TitleContainer and constructs the object in TypeScript, and no cna_content_manager_* route is imported at all. Registering a loader whose product could never be retrieved would be a mechanism with no consumer. Adopting it means projecting CNA's own ContentManager as a second content path with its own cache, which is an architectural decision to take deliberately rather than as a side effect of wanting one registry. The callback shape is not the obstacle: a trampoline holding a napi_ref and a checked slot table would keep void* and function pointers entirely inside the bridge, the same way the text-input subscriptions already do

entries.operation: SpriteFont.MeasureString, checked against CNA's own SpriteFont
entries.evidence: Not checked against numbers somebody typed. CNA's SpriteFont is built over the same texture and the same glyph table and asked the same question, so twenty-four strings are measured twice by implementations that share no code. The font is built to make the corners load-bearing: a negative left bearing, a negative right bearing, unequal cropping heights and a non-zero Spacing. All twenty-four agree exactly at ABI 0.35: the five strings ending in a negative right bearing, which CNA used to count into the width, now measure as XNA's SpriteFont::InternalMeasure does (Math.Max(pending, 0) at each line break and after the loop) -- upstream finding 27, fixed -- and are kept as the cases that would show it again.

entries.operation: Build-time content compilation: source files into .cnb, in a separate package
entries.evidence: The direction docs/content-pipeline-boundary.md chose, built. `cna-ts-content` is a separate package with its own exports, and the runtime tarball contains none of it: the three routes in the whole binding that read a file by path live there and nowhere else, which is what keeps the browser runtime free of filesystem and compiler APIs. Bytes cross that boundary and handles do not -- each operation imports, describes, encodes and releases inside one native call -- so the package owns no native lifetime at all. Proved end to end: a PNG and a RIFF/WAVE file written from their own specifications (not produced by CNA, because an importer test in which CNA reads back its own output proves nothing) are compiled to .cnb, written to disk, and loaded by the real runtime, where the four exact texels and the exact sample bytes come back. The colour key is asserted at the texel: the keyed one becomes transparent and the other three are untouched. Wrong-format sources are refused in both directions, and a planted defect that accepted the colour key without applying it passed until the test stopped varying the content name as well

entries.operation: Camera frame capture

Every injectable state round-trips, and CNA refuses Closed and NotSupported for a device it opened; the injection hooks refuse a camera that is not the test backend. The platform camera is the host's: at ABI 0.35 CNA initialises SDL's camera subsystem before enumerating (upstream finding 34, fixed), so this host's camera and headless Chromium's synthetic one are both enumerated, and the tests follow what the host offers.

entries.operation: CNA's content survey: what is under a content root and which XNB readers it needs
entries.evidence: The test builds the root it surveys, from the same fixtures the XNB reader suites use, so the expected reader names are known independently of what the survey answers rather than read back from it. Four assets across two subdirectories come back as the keys ContentManager.Load addresses -- extension stripped, subdirectories kept -- and a loose .png written beside an .xnb is reported as a native extension rather than as a second asset. A texture declares exactly its one reader and a model exactly its five, in the fixture's own order. Reader usage is counted across the whole root: the texture reader is wanted by two files (the atlas, and the model's effect), each distinct name appears once however many files want it, and each carries whether CNA has a reader for it. The limitation is asserted rather than hidden: the same model written twice, raw and LZX-compressed, reports five reader names and none -- the table lives inside the compressed payload and the survey reads headers without decompressing -- so an empty list means unknown, never "needs nothing". An empty root surveys to nothing instead of failing, changing the root re-points the scan, and a name nothing reads answers false rather than throwing. Loading is deliberately absent: CNA's content manager has a cache and an asset identity of its own, and one asset with two owners would break the same-reference guarantee XNA makes and this package's tests pin. See docs/native-content-survey.md

entries.operation: CNB curves and animation clips
entries.evidence: A curve round-trips its two loop modes, its key count and every field of every key, including a continuity that differs between keys -- and then it is checked the way a curve actually matters, by evaluating both the authored and the decoded curve at ten positions including four between the keys, where the tangents and the continuity decide the answer. What comes back is a managed XNA Curve with no native object behind it: the native handle and its key collection are both released inside the decode. An animation clip keeps its handle, because XNA has no clip type to become; its duration, target space, two tracks with different bone indexes and different keyframe counts, and every component of every keyframe -- three vectors of different lengths at different offsets -- are asserted, along with out-of-range refusals and the fact that a curve and a clip refuse each other's containers. Two planted bridge defects, a dropped key continuity and an ignored track index, each fail exactly one test

entries.operation: CNB model: the bone hierarchy, parts and payloads, materials, meshes, skeleton and lights
entries.evidence: CNB's largest schema, read and written through CnbModelData. A reference model with every projected level occupied at once -- two bones in a hierarchy, a part with real vertex and index payloads, a material with distinguishable values in every field and all eight texture slots named differently, a mesh, a skeleton with three matrix sets, a light -- is built with the public API, encoded by CNA's own writer and decoded back. Every assertion is a value: the exact parent links and transforms, the exact payload bytes and lengths, each of the eight texture names through its own slot, the mesh's parent bone and part membership, and all three skeleton matrix sets kept apart by their own diagonals. Refusals are asserted too: another asset type, a corrupted image, a payload that contradicts its declared part (which CNA validates at encode rather than at set, measured rather than assumed), and use after disposal. Two planted bridge defects -- an ignored skeleton matrix-set identity and an ignored texture slot -- each fail exactly one test

entries.operation: CNB sound effects, songs and videos: the compiled media schemas
entries.evidence: A sound effect round-trips its format, rate, channels, frame count, both loop numbers and its sample bytes exactly, and CNA's own WAV decoder reads a RIFF image into one with the same bytes the header declared; a file that is not a WAV is refused. CreateSoundEffectFromCnb produces a real XNA SoundEffect owning a native audio resource whose name round-trips through CNA, and refuses by name for a format XNA cannot represent -- eight-bit PCM read as sixteen would play as noise -- while leaving the samples readable. Songs and videos carry a stream reference rather than the media, so both schemas are complete and fully testable with no encoded audio or video at all: name, duration and stream reference for a song; dimensions, a non-integer frame rate, duration, soundtrack kind and stream reference for a video. Each of the three refuses the other two's containers. Duration is zero on this artifact because it is built with CNA_AUDIO_PLATFORM=NULL, which is a property of the configuration rather than of the schema; the real 250 ms measurement is made in the browser suite, whose artifact has SDL3 audio

entries.operation: CNB's writers: authoring a container for an asset type CNA has no schema for
entries.evidence: one of every primitive the byte writer offers, decoded back at its exact offset with a DataView -- which is what proves the widths and the little-endian order rather than only that some bytes survived. A u64 survives exactly because it crosses as a bigint; a negative i32 is not read as unsigned; a string carries a four-byte length before its UTF-8 bytes. ToArray copies and Take empties, and the two are distinct. A container built from a custom asset type, custom schema version, metadata, an external reference and a game-defined chunk parses back through the same CnbDocument reader every projected schema uses, with the chunk payload byte for byte. CNB validates structure when a chunk is added -- alignment must be a power of two within its ceiling -- and sizes when the document is built, and both halves are asserted where they happen. Four planted defects all fail: a Take that copies, a u16 written at 32 bits, a dropped power-of-two check, and a limit narrowed but never sent

entries.operation: Compass and motion sensors: absence, and a real reading through CNA's own injection
entries.evidence: Absence first, and it is the point of the family: a heading of zero and a rotation rate of zero are both perfectly plausible measurements, so all three sensors report NotSupported with no valid data and refuse CurrentValue rather than returning them. Then the data path, through cna_compass_set_test_backend_ext and cna_motion_set_test_backend_ext -- CNA's own synthetic backends -- which is **injection evidence, not hardware evidence**: no physical compass or motion sensor exists on this host. Every component carries a value no other component has, so a transposed or substituted field is visible: two compass headings that differ by the local declination, a magnetometer vector, a 16-value attitude matrix asserted by first row and diagonal, a quaternion, and three motion vectors with disjoint value sets. Timestamps cross as bigints and are asserted to the tick, which a double would lose. The north-reference flag is installed both ways and read back both ways, so it is proved read rather than defaulted. A backend cannot be swapped underneath a running acquisition. Three planted defects each fail the test: two headings read from one field, a transposed attitude matrix, and gravity read from the device acceleration

entries.operation: Compiled Effect creation binding route
entries.evidence: exact byte payload reaches cna_effect_create_compiled with compiler-verified ABI; three legal conformance-FXB attempts deterministically return the qualified HEADLESS result 6 with invalid output and no shader-execution claim, and the same payload succeeds on the windowed build

entries.operation: Compiled-effect execution, by renderer
entries.evidence: the capability is a renderer property and was read from the running binary rather than from the renderer's name: CNA_GRAPHICS_CAPABILITY_COMPILED_EFFECTS is false on HEADLESS and true on the windowed OPENGLES3 build. On the windowed one XNA's own BasicEffect.fxb and the CnaConformanceEffect.fxb both load through cna_effect_create_compiled; on HEADLESS the same bytes are refused with result 6 and no shader-execution claim is made. The earlier inventory said only that the bit reports unavailable, which was true of the headless backend and too broad for the qualified set. The browser artifact was asked the same question with the same bytes rather than assumed to match: it answers CNA result 6, naming GraphicsCapability::CompiledEffects as false, which is the same result and sentence the Node HEADLESS backend gives. That answer was unreachable until cna_effect_create_compiled was added to the WebAssembly slice -- the binding declined first, with a message about its own coverage, so a consumer whose artifact HAD the runtime would have been told the wrong thing. WEBGL2 is in the family CNA supports; this artifact is built with CNA_EASYGL_COMPILED_EFFECTS=OFF, which is a build option and is recorded as one. Five backends have now been asked the same bytes and each answers once: OPENGLES3 (EasyGL, built CNA_EASYGL_COMPILED_EFFECTS=ON) creates the effect; SDL_RENDERER, SOFTWARE, HEADLESS and the WEBGL2 browser artifact all refuse with CNA result 6 naming GraphicsCapability::CompiledEffects false. The compiled-effect suite gates on that answer rather than on the word 'windowed': pointing CNA_WINDOWED_LIBRARY at one of the refusing renderers used to fail it with a cascade of assertion errors about missing reflection, and now skips once with the capability the renderer lacks -- while a REQUIRED run still fails, because a gate claiming compiled effects were qualified must not pass on a renderer that has none

entries.operation: Compiled-effect execution: the reflected parameters reach the pixels
entries.evidence: Reflection and write-through above prove a value reaches CNA; they say nothing about it reaching the shader. Measured on the windowed OPENGLES3 build against CnaConformanceEffect.fxb, whose HLSL source CNA ships beside it, so every expectation is computed from the shader's own arithmetic and the values the test sets -- never from GetValue*, which answers from managed state and would agree with its own setter either way. SecondTechnique/P1 returns Tint * Weights[1] and samples nothing: three parameter states, each independently predicted and each matching the eight-bit texel to within one byte, where A->B moves only Tint and B->C only Weights[1]. FirstTechnique/P0 is a different program over identical parameter state -- it samples a white texel and scales by Gain and the Lighting struct -- so its disagreement with P1 is what makes CurrentTechnique's selection evidence; Lighting.Intensity and Lighting.Thresholds[0] are a struct member and a struct array element that only the pixel changes could prove. Halving Gain alone halves that image. A freshly constructed effect's FIRST draw is already correct, which is the opposite of what upstream finding 22 records for a ShaderEffect through SpriteBatch, and nothing here primes anything; a multiple-render-target bind straight after a compiled-effect draw also succeeds, where finding 22's pending GL error refuses it. Eight planted defects -- four dropped write-throughs, a truncated array, a no-op Apply, an ignored technique and a zeroed Vector4 W -- all fail these tests, against a rebuilt artifact, with the source and the artifact proved back at their baseline hash. This states what one fixture on one renderer proves and does not generalise to every compiled effect. Measured on two rasterizers rather than one: the AMD Radeon 780M (radeonsi) and Mesa's llvmpipe under Xvfb, both through the same OPENGLES3 EasyGL build. The expectations are unchanged between them and were written with a one-byte tolerance from the start, so this evidence is a property of the shader's arithmetic rather than of this machine's GPU -- which two neighbouring tests, having pinned exact bytes, turned out not to be

entries.operation: Compiled-effect parameter reflection and shader write-through
entries.evidence: Effect.Parameters used to be built empty for a natively reflected effect. A stock effect's native collection really is empty on both backends -- measured -- so the surface looked unreachable; a compiled effect on a renderer that can run one carries the real thing. XNA's BasicEffect.fxb reflects twenty-three parameters with their names, classes, types, row and column counts, the 32-element VSIndices and PSIndices arrays, and Texture as an Object/Texture2D. SetValue is proved to reach CNA rather than managed state alone by reading the value back through cna_effect_parameter_get_value: a Matrix, a Vector4 and a scalar each arrive component for component. A value shape CNA's tagged API cannot carry is refused by name rather than stored and dropped

entries.operation: Custom shader effects: an Effect built from GLSL the game wrote itself
entries.evidence: a ShaderEffect IS an Effect -- asserted with instanceof, and with the one technique and one pass it reports -- so it goes wherever a stock effect goes, which is the whole point of it. All three IEffectMatrices transforms round-trip to distinct values, and are read AGAIN after every uniform setter has run, so a setter wired to one of them instead of to its own uniform is caught. Every uniform shape CNA offers is exercised: mat4, vec4, vec3, vec2, float, int, float array, vec2 array, vec3 array, mat4 array and the std140 block declaration with its clearing form. The refusals are this binding's own and each names a different mistake: an empty or missing uniform name, a value that is not finite, a block whose names and offsets differ in length, and an array argument that is not one. A texture bound to a sampler unit is LENT to the effect -- the texture then refuses disposal while the effect can sample it, and disposes cleanly once the effect is gone, so the order is the only thing that matters -- and on a windowed renderer a texture bound to unit 1 is what a shader sampling unit 1 reads, which a binding that went to unit 0 cannot produce. Nonsense source is handled the way CNA's header says it must be: success means the object exists and not that anything compiled, and the two renderers here disagree exactly as the header predicts -- HEADLESS reports it valid with an empty log because it never compiled it, OPENGLES3 reports it invalid with the compiler's own words. Two empty sources are the one case refused identically everywhere; one empty source is not. On a windowed renderer the effect drives real pixels, and the weighted-blended accumulation it makes possible is predicted channel by channel from the published weight. Upstream finding 22 is asserted rather than worked around: a fresh effect's FIRST SpriteBatch draw produces nothing, its second is correct, a separately created effect loses its own first draw too, the same batch with no custom effect draws correctly the first time, and one Apply outside any batch fixes it -- which is the diagnosis as much as the workaround. Seventeen planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: Destroying a test-backend camera, then opening the platform one
entries.evidence: Fixed in CNA ABI 0.35 (upstream finding 11). At 0.21 cna_camera_destroy freed a test-backend camera without clearing the process-wide platform override that pointed into it, so the next platform camera crashed. The native suite now runs the sequence in a child process and asserts it survives; the browser suite asserts the same after enumerating cameras.

entries.operation: Direct standalone GraphicsDevice construction
entries.evidence: XNA public GraphicsDevice constructor now creates a real second device beside the game one, with no game of its own: cna_graphics_device_create takes an adapter index and presentation parameters and nothing else. A Texture2D made on it round-trips its four exact texels, its viewport and presentation parameters are its own rather than the manager (64x48 against the game 320x240), two caller-created devices live at once each answering with its own profile and size, and a texture from one device is refused by another device SpriteBatch with InvalidOperationException. The ownership rule is asserted directly off the native lifetime rather than inferred from a symptom: a caller-created device releases its own handle exactly once, and disposing a manager-created device leaves the game native lifetime active -- a Dispose that released whatever lifetime it found passed every other assertion and is caught only by that one. The description and device name are CNA's canonical XNA values rather than a GPU probe -- the same on HEADLESS and OPENGLES3 -- and that is stated rather than dressed up. entries.operation: MediaLibrary over CNA's index of the user's Music and Pictures folders
entries.evidence: The library was projected with empty collections; it is not empty. The test builds the folders it then reads, so every expected value is known independently of what the library reports: a WAV of exactly 4000 frames at 8000Hz reports exactly 500ms -- a duration read from the file rather than defaulted, which a zero would have passed a weaker test with -- its containing folder becomes the album, a cover.png beside it becomes real album art returned byte for byte, and a 1x1 PNG in the picture root comes back measured 1x1 with its exact pixels. Art and pixels are fetched when asked for, not when the library is opened, because XNA asks for them with a method for that reason. SavePicture writes a picture that a re-opened library finds, and the token CNA gives it resolves through the public GetPictureFromToken to that very object. entries.operation: The debug drawer: lines and shapes, read back as geometry
entries.evidence: everything the drawer draws is a line list and cna_debug_draw_copy_vertices hands the whole list back, so what a shape consists of is read rather than looked at -- which is why this family needs no renderer to be qualified. A line is exactly its two endpoints in order; a cross is three lines reaching its size along each axis and nowhere else; a box is twelve edges over eight corners, asserted as the exact ordered edge list over a box asymmetric in all three axes so that a swapped Min and Max is a different picture rather than the same corners reordered, with each corner used by exactly three edges. A sphere is three rings of its segment count, every vertex exactly on the sphere and on one of the three axis planes through its centre, and twice the segments is twice the lines; a BoundingSphere draws exactly what the same centre and radius draw. A frustum's twelve edges use all eight of the corners BoundingFrustum gives for the same matrix and nothing else -- a second independent implementation, as with the frustum culler. The gizmos are checked against the light they describe: a point light is a sphere at exactly its range plus a cross, a spot light is two cones whose rims are at range times the tangent of the outer and the inner angle on the plane the range reaches, and a directional light is an arrow starting a length back along its direction with a head a fixed fraction of that length. The depth-tested and overlay lists are separate and keep their own colours including alpha, the line count is both together, clearing empties both, and beginning a frame starts it empty. Seven planted binding defects fail and none survives

entries.operation: The Guide's two asynchronous screens, and CNA's own answers to them
entries.evidence: Guide.BeginShowMessageBox and Guide.BeginShowKeyboardInput are the only genuinely asynchronous begin/end pairs in XNA, and both now work. A message box does not complete inside the Begin call and says so, carries the caller's async state untouched, makes Guide.IsVisible true, and holds the focus button XNA was given rather than a default. Answering it runs the continuation exactly once with the very result object Begin returned -- the IAsyncResult contract -- and EndShowMessageBox returns the button that was pressed; a second box with a different press returns that one instead, so the answer is not a constant. The keyboard input reports its title, description and starting text back from CNA, and a cancel makes EndShowKeyboardInput return null rather than an empty string, which is XNA's distinction. A second screen while one is pending is INVALID_STATE, and End before the answer is an error rather than a wait. Three planted defects fail: a dropped focus button, an End that accepts a foreign or incomplete result, and a continuation that fires twice. Nothing here fabricates a gamer, a sign-in or a peer: CNA draws the screen and answers it, which is the same deterministic injection the sensors and the camera use

The engine layer is deliberately absent: the WebAssembly artifact is built CNA_CNAEXT=OFF, so every instanced renderer and LOD route answers NOT_SUPPORTED there -- measured -- and binding them would offer a capability that cannot work. entries.operation: Browser GamePad: connection, capabilities, buttons, thumbsticks and triggers
entries.evidence: test/wasm-browser-input.mjs drives GamePad.GetState/GetCapabilities from inside an ordinary XNA Update in headless Chromium. With no controller attached all four PlayerIndex slots report IsConnected false rather than an invented device; with a Gamepad API device emulated at the browser boundary -- the integration point SDL3's Emscripten joystick driver actually reads -- the capability table, A and D-pad button states, both thumbstick axes with CNA's Y-inversion, the analog left trigger and an advancing PacketNumber all arrive, and releasing returns every one of them to zero. SetVibration reports false, because the browser's standard mapping exposes no rumble to SDL. Three planted defects -- swapped thumbsticks, an always-connected capability table and a previous-position that reports the current one -- each fail exactly one of these tests

entries.operation: Browser GameWindow: title, client bounds and the resize event
entries.evidence: The XNA GameWindow over the canvas CNA presents to. The title round-trips through CNA, the orientation and screen device name answer, and Window.Handle is CNA own native-window token passed through unchanged rather than a fabricated pointer. A device change through GraphicsDeviceManager.ApplyChanges of a known delta moves ClientBounds by exactly that delta, raises ClientSizeChanged once, and a handler attached at the time reads the new bounds; restoring the preferred size restores them

entries.operation: Browser GraphicsAdapter read through a live device
entries.evidence: GraphicsAdapter.Adapters, DefaultAdapter and GraphicsDevice.Adapter all answer in a browser, filled from CNA own adapter routes rather than invented. Nothing here manufactures a display name: what the Emscripten platform calls its adapter is what a consumer gets. What is asserted is consistency -- the current display mode has a positive size, its aspect ratio is its own width over its own height, the wide-screen flag agrees with that ratio rather than with a neighbouring field, the adapter reports at least the mode it is in as supported, and the device adapter is the first listed one

entries.operation: Browser Guide: message box and keyboard input, with exactly-once completion
entries.evidence: No modal opens anywhere: CNA holds its own pending dialog and draws it itself, which is what makes the asynchronous contract checkable in headless Chromium. A message box is begun, reports itself pending with the focus button it was given, is clicked through CNA simulate route, and its End reports that button with the completion handler having run exactly once; ending the same token twice is refused as the Node bridge refuses it. A keyboard prompt carries its title, description and default text to CNA, is cancelled, and its End answers null rather than the empty string a game would read as a deliberately blank name. Guide.SimulateTrialMode round-trips and does not move IsTrialMode, which the pinned XNA IL confirms is correct: they are two independent static fields

entries.operation: Browser media player state and an empty media library
entries.evidence: The media player mute, repeat, shuffle, volume and visualisation flags all reach CNA, the platform reports its local media source by name, and the game has control. The visualisation buffers are read at their measured length -- 256 floats each -- and with nothing playing they are zero, which is recorded as silence rather than dressed up as a spectrum. What used to end there now continues: the visualisation is a post-mix tap on CNA whole mixer rather than on the media player own track, so an XACT cue, a SoundEffect and a DynamicSoundEffectInstance all reach it, and four authored tones each land in the bin round(f * 512 / rate) predicts from their own frequency and the rate CNA mixer announced. The magnitude is predicted too, from the transform own documented scaling -- 2/N with the Hann window 0.5 coherent gain left uncompensated, so amplitude/2 -- and the two page-authored tones sit exactly on a bin centre where the window response is textbook: half the peak in each adjacent bin, essentially nothing two bins out. The frequency axis itself is upstream finding 35: CNA does not publish the mixer negotiated rate on the C ABI, and the browser own AudioContext runs at a different rate (48000 against 44100), so the suite takes it from CNA stderr notice and asserts the two really do differ. The media library opens and reports zero of all seven collections, which on a host with no music or pictures folder is the correct answer; an index into an empty collection is refused

entries.operation: Browser microphones: enumeration, buffer duration and capture state
entries.evidence: SDL3 Emscripten backend enumerates recording devices, and headless Chromium reports two -- a default device and a system audio recording device -- each with a name, a 44100 Hz sample rate, a state and a buffer duration, and exactly one of them marked default. A buffer duration written is the duration read back as a 64-bit tick count, starting and stopping move the state, and a capture asks for 65536 bytes and is answered with what CNA produced rather than with what was asked for. The old row stopped there, at PHYSICAL_CAPTURE_NOT_VERIFIED, because a page needs microphone permission. It does -- and Chromium can supply a capture device that is not hardware at all. Launched with --use-fake-device-for-media-stream and --use-file-for-fake-audio-capture pointing at a file this repository authored, every capture device Chromium offers is synthetic, and what CNA records is that file: two tones at 1500 Hz and 3187.5 Hz, present at the 2:1 amplitude ratio they were written at, at least ten times above anything else in the spectrum (measured 50:1). Chromium own gain control costs about 20 dB of absolute level and leaves the ratio alone, so the assertions are on the shape, which room noise, a buffer of zeroes and a single hard-coded frequency all fail. SYNTHETIC_BROWSER_CAPTURE_VERIFIED. PHYSICAL_MICROPHONE_ACCESSED = 0 and PHYSICAL_CAPTURE_VERIFIED = 0: the harness refuses to launch without the file flag rather than falling back to a real device, and a synthetic device passing is not evidence that a physical one would. Two things had to be found on the way: Playwright bundled headless shell has no media-capture stack at all, so the run asks for the full chromium channel by name, and SDL3 recording backend writes zeroes on a timer until its own getUserMedia resolves, so a capture that stopped at the first buffer would read that silence as a microphone that delivered nothing. BufferDuration is upstream finding 28

entries.operation: Browser off-screen rendering with exact pixel readback
entries.evidence: a RenderTarget2D is created, bound, cleared to an exact colour and read back through Texture2D.GetData in headless Chromium on WebGL2; all sixteen texels equal the cleared value, and disposing a still-bound target is refused

entries.operation: Browser sensors driven through CNA synthetic backends
entries.evidence: SYNTHETIC_BACKEND_VERIFIED, not PHYSICAL_SENSOR_VERIFIED. All four sensors report unsupported on headless Chromium and a reading from an unsupported sensor is refused rather than answered with zeroes. Each is then driven through CNA own test backend: an accelerometer interval written and read back as a 64-bit tick count, a compass reading injected and returned with its three doubles distinct, its magnetometer axes and signs intact and a timestamp that a JavaScript double could not hold, a gyroscope rate keeping its signs, and a fused motion reading whose attitude quaternion, sixteen-float rotation matrix, three vectors and own nested timestamp all survive. CNA validates the timestamp pair as a real DateTimeOffset: an offset that is not a whole number of minutes is refused

entries.operation: Browser sound effects: PCM construction, exact duration and the instance state machine
entries.evidence: a quarter second of 16-bit mono PCM built in the page reports exactly 250 ms and 2,500,000 ticks, volume, pitch, pan and looping round-trip through CNA at float precision, and an instance walks stopped -> playing -> paused -> playing -> stopped. Audibility is deliberately not claimed, and the reason has been corrected. A browser really will not start a WebAudio context without a user gesture -- measured: a fresh AudioContext is suspended at load and a page-initiated element.click() is isTrusted false and leaves it suspended -- but that gates output rather than mixing, and this suite had been getting an activation by accident anyway, because Playwright issues CDP Runtime.evaluate with userGesture true so page.evaluate and page.waitForFunction grant one. test/wasm-browser-audio.mjs supplies a deliberate one instead and measures both halves apart. SoundEffect.Play reports whether the runtime accepted the sample; whether anyone heard it is not something a headless browser can answer

entries.operation: Browser storage: containers, directories, files and pattern listing
entries.evidence: StorageDevice selection, a container opened by name and answering with it, a directory and two files created, both listed, a search pattern that reaches CNA and returns one of the two, a file read back, and a file and a directory that stop existing when deleted. Opening a file that is not there is refused rather than answered with empty bytes. The filesystem is the module own: in-session behaviour is what is verified here and persistence across a page reload is not claimed, because that is the host page IDBFS decision rather than this binding

entries.operation: Browser text composition and the extended input inventory
entries.evidence: A committed UTF-16 code unit raised through CNA arrives at a subscription as its character, including U+263A which a byte mask would truncate; a composition update keeps its text and selection; a candidate list keeps its order, selection and orientation; and an unsubscribed handler stops being called, which is the module function-table entry actually being released. Headless Chromium reports zero joysticks and zero haptic devices and refuses an index past the end of either

entries.operation: Browser title storage and ContentManager XNB loading
entries.evidence: the browser harness writes assets into the module filesystem, reads exact title bytes back through TitleContainer.OpenStream, and loads an uncompressed Texture2D XNB and an LZX-compressed SpriteFont XNB through an ordinary ContentManager; a missing asset refuses with CNA_RESULT_IO rather than reading as empty

entries.operation: Browser TouchPanel: the touch collection and XNA's press/move/release states
entries.evidence: test/wasm-browser-input.mjs dispatches real Chromium touch events and reads TouchPanel.GetState from inside Update. Before the first finger there is no touch device at all, which is distinct from a device with nothing on it. A press arrives as TouchLocationState.Pressed with no previous location, the next frame is Moved at the same point, a move keeps the identifier and reports the press position as its previous one, a second finger is Pressed while the first stays Moved, and lifting reports Released exactly once before the collection empties. The XNA enumerator visits the same identifiers in the same order as the indexer

entries.operation: Browser VideoPlayer control surface
entries.evidence: A player is created, holds looping, mute and volume, reports its state and position, and is destroyed. Its frame reports itself unavailable with CNA invalid handle and a zero generation, and playing a null video is refused -- claiming a frame with no decoder is the one thing this family must not do. Decoding itself is not available on this toolchain at all and is recorded separately

entries.operation: Browser WebAudio rendering behind a browser-trusted user activation
entries.evidence: The gesture rule is real and it was being satisfied by accident. Measured with no CDP call having touched the page: a fresh AudioContext is suspended at load, a page-initiated element.click() is isTrusted false and grants neither sticky nor transient activation and leaves it suspended, and a Playwright locator.click() is isTrusted true, grants both, and moves SDL own context from suspended to running. The accident is that Playwright issues CDP Runtime.evaluate with userGesture true, so page.evaluate and page.waitForFunction GRANT an activation -- every other browser suite here has been handing its page a gesture it never asked for, and a pre-gesture measurement read that way would have been measuring the question. So the harness gained an HTTP page-to-harness channel and runFrames(frames, page, { activate: true }), which waits on that channel and then sends a real click; the pre-gesture facts come back over HTTP before Playwright has run a line of script in the page. What the gesture does NOT gate is mixing: SDL3 Emscripten backend, finding the context suspended, pumps the audio callback from a timer and discards the buffer, so CNA mixer runs either way and the pre-gesture and post-gesture spectra of the same cue are identical to every digit. A second observable owes nothing to this package arithmetic -- DynamicSoundEffectInstance.PendingBufferCount drains 6 to 0 as CNA mixer finishes with the buffers, which is CNA counting its own consumption. WEB_AUDIO_RENDERING_VERIFIED and XACT_SAMPLE_CONSUMPTION_VERIFIED; AUDIBLE_OUTPUT_VERIFIED = 0, because a headless browser has no speaker and no amount of local work changes that

entries.operation: Browser/Wasm CNA runtime
entries.evidence: 60 and 600 real frames of the public XNA Game/GraphicsDeviceManager/Texture2D/SpriteBatch path in headless Chromium on a WebGL2 context, ABI 0.35.0, no uncaught page error

entries.operation: CNA device layer over WebAssembly: host, locales, clipboard and a synthetic camera
entries.evidence: Present on an artifact built CNA_DEVICES=ON and reporting itself absent on one that is not, with both branches asserted. Where present: logical cores, system memory, power state, content scale and the display safe area all answer; the preferred-locale list answers with a language tag that is one; the device-layer clipboard write reports whether the platform accepted it. The camera is CNA own test backend and is labelled SYNTHETIC_BACKEND_VERIFIED -- a 4x2 frame keeps both of its dimensions, each state the backend accepts is the state it then reports, and CNA refuses to be told a camera it opened is closed

entries.operation: CNA's graphics extensions over WebAssembly: every public extension class, and the ASCII quantizer's texels
entries.evidence: on an artifact built with CNA_CNAEXT=ON, headless Chromium on WebGL2 constructs every public extension class -- the PBR and skinned PBR effects, the CRT and depth effects, the ASCII effect and the debug drawer -- reads every accessor and round-trips every settable one, and draws the ASCII quantizer over four uniform quadrants with every texel predicted from AsciiQuantizer.cpp: three dark quadrants exactly their cell background, the white one exactly its two named colours, the collapsed cell its average, and BlackWhite mode with no hue.

entries.operation: CNB curves and animation clips in a browser
entries.evidence: the same two schemas over the WebAssembly backend, and the one that settles a wasm32 convention with evidence: cna_curve_key_collection_add takes CNA_CurveKey **by value**, and cna_cnb_encode_animation_clip takes a descriptor holding a pointer to an array of descriptors each holding a pointer to an array of 48-byte keyframes. Both cross correctly -- the page's decoded curve evaluates identically to the one it authored at ten sample positions, and every keyframe component of both clip tracks comes back exactly. All the layouts involved are measured by the Emscripten probe rather than written

entries.operation: CNB in a browser: the same compiled-content API, on the WebAssembly backend
entries.evidence: a page encodes a texture with CNA's own writer, parses the container back and uploads it with CreateTexture2DFromCnb, and the four readback texels are exactly the RGBA the encoder was given -- the same assertion the Node suite makes, through the same public API, against a different backend. The container primitives agree across backends too: the CRC-32C check value and the magic are the same C routines either side

entries.operation: CNB media in a browser, including a measured sound-effect duration
entries.evidence: the same three schemas over the WebAssembly backend. The browser artifact is built with SDL3 audio rather than NULL, so this is where the sound effect's duration is actually measurable: a quarter second of 8 kHz mono PCM16 encoded to .cnb, decoded back and turned into an XNA SoundEffect reports exactly 250 ms and 2,500,000 ticks, which is arithmetic on the frame count and therefore exact evidence that the samples and the rate both survived. Both loop numbers, the sample bytes, and the song and video descriptions are asserted as on Node

entries.operation: CNB model in a browser: the same schema, on the WebAssembly backend
entries.evidence: a page builds a model with CnbModelData, encodes it with CNA's own writer and decodes it back, asserting the same values the Node suite asserts: both bone parents and both transforms, the part's stride and its exact vertex and index payloads through wasm32 memory, two named texture slots beside a third left empty, the mesh's parent bone and part list, all three skeleton matrix sets kept apart by their own diagonals, and the baked light. The structure layouts are measured by the same Emscripten probe as the rest, never hand-written. A planted defect that ignored the skeleton matrix-set identity fails this test; a second, which returned zero for every bone parent, passed until the test was strengthened to sample the root bone as well as the child -- so the gate is known to be able to fail for both

entries.operation: CNB's writers produce identical bytes on both backends
entries.evidence: the content-pipeline boundary claims a .cnb built in a build script and one built in a page are the same bytes. A browser page builds the same 52-byte payload and the same 326-byte container from the same calls, and the test compares the payload against the exact little-endian layout the desktop ABI produces rather than against the page agreeing with itself. The read-limits structure crosses through a wasm32 layout measured by an Emscripten probe, not a handwritten one

entries.operation: Compiled XNA Effect reflection, native parameter write-through, technique selection and rendered pixels, over WebAssembly
entries.evidence: Available only on an artifact built with CNA_EASYGL_COMPILED_EFFECTS=ON; the default artifact answers CNA_RESULT_NOT_SUPPORTED naming GraphicsCapability::CompiledEffects, and the browser suite asserts that refusal instead. On a strong artifact, headless Chromium on WebGL2 loads CnaConformanceEffect.fxb through the ordinary XNA Effect constructor, reflects its six parameters with their classes, types and array/struct shape, writes values that CNA reads back, selects both techniques, and draws texels matching arithmetic computed from CNA's own shipped HLSL to within a byte -- the same scenario and the same expectation the windowed OPENGLES3 suite is held to. Fourteen planted defects die on it.

entries.operation: Device capability and compute work-group limit queries over WebAssembly
entries.evidence: All nineteen GraphicsCapability identities and the three compute work-group limits, asked of a live WebGL2 device through the public GraphicsDeviceCapabilities. Sixteen of nineteen are on for the default artifact and seventeen for one built with CNA_EASYGL_COMPILED_EFFECTS=ON -- CompiledEffects is the only one that moves, which is a second and independent confirmation of the compiled-effect capability, reached without touching the Effect constructor. ComputeShaders and IndirectDraw are off on both and no CNA build option changes them: WebGL 2.0 has no compute stage and no indirect draw, so every engine family needing either is renderer-blocked rather than unbound. This slice dispatches nothing; compute shaders, storage buffers, image bindings, barriers and GPU timers all refuse by name.

entries.operation: Modern CNA runtime services over WebAssembly
entries.evidence: the browser harness reads platform, renderer selection and available renderers, and round-trips two by-value CNA_StringView routes

entries.operation: SpriteFont measurement checked against CNA over WebAssembly
entries.evidence: CNA SpriteFont built in a browser over the same texture and the same glyph table the managed font holds, and asked for twenty-four strings. The two implementations share no code and agree exactly on all of them at ABI 0.35, including the five that upstream finding 27 used to split. The oracle is shared with the Node suite, so a browser answering differently is a failure rather than a second green suite.

entries.operation: Standalone GraphicsDevice construction in a browser
entries.evidence: XNA's public GraphicsDevice constructor in a browser: a real second device at the 64x48 its presentation parameters asked for rather than the game's size, which disposes, after which the game still disposes cleanly. It was withdrawn once because on CNA before 17281e841 the game's destroy then threw an Emscripten ErrnoError (errno 44) from SDL's file-drop teardown -- upstream finding 32, fixed by CNA for Emscripten -- and the WebAssembly backend now implements both halves and the browser suite asserts the device and the clean disposal

entries.operation: WebAssembly game lifecycle, device creation, Clear, Texture2D transfer, SpriteBatch and input snapshots
entries.evidence: test/wasm-browser.mjs drives the first vertical slice through the same public XNA classes the Node backend serves

entries.operation: XACT in a browser over repository-authored banks
entries.evidence: The settings file, wave bank and sound bank are written from scratch by test/fixtures/xact.mjs rather than downloaded, so the family is not fixture-blocked: CNA parses real XACT bytes. An engine loads two categories and two global variables, the writable one takes a new value and the READONLY one does not, the renderer list answers, two fetches of one category are two handles that CNA own comparison and hash agree are equal, and a cue runs prepared then playing then paused-while-playing then playing then stopped. A cue name that is not in the bank is refused. Two authored cues are then run into CNA mixer and measured: 261.6 Hz answers bin 3 and 523.3 Hz answers bin 6, each predicted by round(f * 512 / 44100) rather than recorded, at the amplitude the visualisation transform own scaling implies, with silence before the cue and silence after it. That measurement is what found the fixture own defect: it wrote nChannels = 0 into the wave bank MINIWAVEFORMAT on the belief that the field holds the count minus one, and CNA reads it as (channels == 1) ? Mono : Stereo, so every mono wave here had been decoding as interleaved stereo and playing at exactly double its authored frequency. Nothing had ever measured the pitch. Audibility is still not claimed, but the user gesture is no longer the reason: a browser-trusted Playwright click is supplied, the AudioContext leaves suspended for running, and the pre-gesture and post-gesture spectra are identical -- SDL3 Emscripten backend pumps the mixer from a timer while the context is suspended and discards the output, so the gesture gates output and not mixing. What remains unproved is that a speaker moved, and a headless browser has none
